title: Minimal Python Agent Harness Architecture
relationships: System Prompt Assembly (1) flows into the Execution Loop (2) as the entry point
The Execution Loop (2) branches out to Context Management (3), Pre-Tool Hooks (4), and Session Persistence (9)
Pre-Tool Hooks (4) feed into Permissions & Safety (5), which then feed Tool Registry Dispatch (6)
Tool Registry Dispatch (6) branches into Built-in Primitives (7) and Sub-Agent Management (8)
visual_elements: Outer container rectangle with a blue-to-magenta gradient border enclosing all nodes
White rounded boxes each outlined with the same blue-to-pink gradient and a soft drop shadow
Bold black directional arrows showing a top-down tree/flow structure
Two visible branching points (one 3-way at the loop, one 2-way at dispatch)
Light near-white background with centered dark sans-serif labels inside each box
key_points: The harness is a layered pipeline: prompt setup drives a bounded while-loop that gates every tool call
Safety is two-staged — pre-tool hooks (allow/deny/modify) precede a permission level (read-only/workspace/full)
Tool dispatch splits work into local primitives versus spawned sub-agents, separating single-step actions from delegated tasks
Context management and session persistence act as side channels that run alongside the main dispatch path
Numbering the nine boxes gives learners a concrete checklist for building a minimal agent from scratch

title: Harness Execution Loop Process
components: Final Answer (No Tool Calls Text Response)
relationships: Initialize Session flows into Read Context, then Call LLM, then Evaluate Output
Evaluate Output branches: 'No Tool Calls' leads to Final Answer; 'Tool Calls' leads to Execute Tool
Execute Tool -> Append Observation -> Increment Turn -> Check Iteration Limit
Check Iteration Limit branches: 'Max Reached' leads to Max Limit Exceeded; 'Not Max' loops back to Read Context
Both Final Answer and Max Limit Exceeded converge into Task Complete
visual_elements: Blue rounded process boxes each containing a small icon and a two-line label
Two orange hexagonal decision nodes (Evaluate Output, Check Iteration Limit)
Branch labels in blue text on the arrows (No Tool Calls / Tool Calls / Max Reached / Not Max)
A long bottom feedback line that loops from Check Iteration Limit back to before Read Context
Two terminal exit paths converging on a single Task Complete node
key_points: The harness is fundamentally a loop: call the model, inspect the output, then either finish or run tools and repeat
There are exactly two exit conditions: a clean final answer (no tool calls) or a hard stop when the iteration limit is exceeded
Each iteration mutates state by appending tool observations to the message array and bumping a turn counter
Decision nodes (orange hexagons) gate the flow and are the only points where the path can diverge
Looping back to Read Context (not to Call LLM) ensures the freshly assembled context is what the next inference sees

title: Agent Harness Execution Loop
relationships: Initialize Agent flows into the Iteration < Max? decision
Iteration < Max? --Yes--> Read & Call Model
Iteration < Max? --No--> Raise TimeoutError (loop termination on limit)
Read & Call Model flows into the Has Tool Calls? decision
Has Tool Calls? --No--> Return Final Answer (happy-path exit)
Has Tool Calls? --Yes--> Execute Tool Calls
Execute Tool Calls flows into Observe Results
Observe Results loops back up the right edge to re-enter the Iteration < Max? check
visual_elements: Light-blue rounded rectangles for action/terminal steps
Orange diamond shapes for the two decision points (Iteration < Max? and Has Tool Calls?)
Dark directional arrows with Yes/No branch labels at each fork
A long right-side loop-back line from Observe Results returning to the top of the iteration check
Bold centered title 'Agent Harness Execution Loop' above the diagram
key_points: The harness runs a bounded loop, checking a max-iteration guard before each model call to prevent runaway agents; exceeding it raises a TimeoutError
Each cycle reads the prompt and calls the model, then inspects the response for requested tool calls
If the model emits no tool calls, the loop exits cleanly and the final answer is returned to the caller
If tool calls are present, they are executed and their outputs are observed, after which control returns to the iteration guard to continue the agentic cycle
The two diamonds encode the control flow: one guards termination, the other decides between finishing and acting
source_file: sec-3-What is an agent harness The nine components of a great one.png

title: Agent Harness Context Compaction Process
relationships: Count Tokens flows into the Tokens < Threshold? decision node
Decision 'Yes' branch bypasses compaction and goes straight to Return Messages
Decision 'No' branch flows into Trigger Compaction
Trigger Compaction fans out in parallel to Extract Prefix, Extract Recent, and Summarize Middle
The three extraction/summarization steps fan back in to Reassemble
Reassemble flows into the final Return Compacted output
visual_elements: Orange hexagon for the threshold decision node contrasting with blue process nodes
Light-blue rounded rectangles each with a small line icon and a two-line caption
Labeled 'Yes' and 'No' edges emerging from the hexagon
A parallel fan-out then fan-in pattern around the three middle processing boxes
Left-to-right horizontal flow with a vertical branch for the three extraction steps
key_points: Compaction is conditional: it only runs when the token count exceeds the budget threshold, giving a cheap fast path otherwise
The prefix (system prompt plus initial user goal) is preserved verbatim to keep identity and intent intact
The most recent turns are kept as working memory so the agent retains immediate context
Only the older middle history is compressed into a summary, which is where the token savings come from
The preserved prefix, fresh summary, and recent turns are reassembled into a new, smaller message list that replaces the original

title: LLM History Compaction Process
relationships: Raw History flows into the token threshold decision node
A 'Yes' branch (over 80% window) routes to LLM summarization of middle blocks
Summarization output flows into Compacted History
A 'No' branch loops from the decision node back to Raw History unchanged
visual_elements: Blue database icon card for Raw History
Orange hexagon decision node for the token threshold
Blue folder icon card for Compacted History
Yes/No labeled branch on the decision node
Curved No-loop arrow returning to the start node
key_points: Compaction triggers only when token usage exceeds 80% of the context window
Middle discussion and stack traces are distilled into a single summary block
Recent turns are kept verbatim and the system prompt cache is preserved
Sub-threshold histories skip summarization and continue unchanged via the No loop
Compaction restores the token budget without losing critical context

title: LLM Tool Execution with Permission Gating
components: LLM Inference Output (tool call request: run_command pytest)
Check Permission Tiers (verify execution is permitted)
Permission Denied Exception (raise error for unauthorized access)
relationships: LLM Inference Output flows into Lookup Tool
Lookup Tool feeds into the Check Permission Tiers decision node
Check Permission Tiers routes to Built-in Shell on the 'Allowed' branch
Check Permission Tiers routes to Permission Denied Exception on the 'Denied' branch
visual_elements: A central orange hexagon representing the permission gate / decision point
Light-blue rounded rectangles for each linear process step
A small icon inside every box (robot, database, shield, terminal, warning)
Branching arrows explicitly labeled 'Allowed' and 'Denied'
Color contrast between the orange gate and the blue pipeline steps
key_points: The harness intercepts the raw LLM tool-call before anything runs
Tool metadata must be resolved before a permission decision can be made
Permission tiers act as a security gate that splits execution into two paths
Approved calls run inside a controlled built-in shell via subprocess.run
Rejected calls short-circuit to a Permission Denied Exception instead of executing

title: Sub-Agent Exploration and Verification Workflow
relationships: A single left-to-right timeline arrow connects all eight steps in sequence
Parent agent triggers both the explorer and verifier spawns as orchestration points
Each spawn is paired with an isolated sub-agent session created by the manager
Explorer session loops through search turns then returns a condensed summary back to the parent
Verifier session runs the test suite (pytest) and returns a pass/fail result to the parent
Layout alternates parent-side actions on the top row with sub-agent-side actions on the bottom row
visual_elements: Central horizontal timeline arrow with small circular node markers at each step
Two staggered rows of rounded rectangular cards (blue, green, yellow, red on top; cyan, green, orange, pink on bottom)
Simple line icons inside each card (agent nodes, search, folder, speech bubble, person, checkmark)
Color-coded heading labels with a two-line caption above each top card and below each bottom card
Clean white background with subtle drop shadows on the cards
key_points: Sub-agents run in isolated, fresh contexts so the parent's context window stays clean
Exploration and verification are split into separate specialized sub-agents rather than one monolithic run
Each sub-agent session is given restricted, role-appropriate tools (e.g. pytest only for the verifier)
Sub-agents return condensed summaries and pass/fail reports instead of raw logs, protecting parent context
The workflow is a strict sequential pipeline: explore, summarize, then verify, then report

title: Session Persistence and Prompt Pipeline Architecture
relationships: Top lane: linear event flow USER_INPUT -> MODEL_CALL -> TOOL_RESULT -> COMPACTION_EVENT -> session_transcript.json
Bottom lane: linear prompt assembly Base Harness Instructions -> Injected AGENTS.md -> Replayed History
Two parallel horizontal lanes: an append-only event log (top) running alongside a context/prompt construction pipeline (bottom)
COMPACTION_EVENT terminates the top lane by flushing summarized events into the green database cylinder
visual_elements: Two parallel horizontal lanes of light-blue rounded rectangles connected by right-pointing arrows
A distinct green database cylinder (session_transcript.json) capping the right end of the top lane
A small monochrome icon embedded in the left of every box (terminal, gears, clock, layers, etc.)
Bold dark title centered above the diagram
Bold cyan step labels paired with smaller grey description text inside each box
key_points: The harness records each turn as a discrete, ordered event (user input, model call, tool result) forming a session log
A compaction step summarizes the event stream and persists it to session_transcript.json for durable storage
The prompt is rebuilt each turn from three layers: static base instructions, dynamically injected AGENTS.md config, and replayed compacted history
Event logging (top) and prompt assembly (bottom) are conceptually separate pipelines that the harness orchestrates together
Compacted history acts as working memory, keeping context bounded while preserving essential state across the session

title: Tool Execution Workflow
relationships: Sequential left-to-right pipeline: each stage loops from its bottom edge up into the top of the next stage
Tool Call Proposed feeds a parsed command into the Dynamic Command Parser
Command Parser routes to the Active Permission Tier based on the detected command tier
Permission Tier either auto-grants (Full Access / Workspace Mode) or escalates to the Interactive User Approval Prompt
User approval gates the final Execution and Audit stage, which runs the subprocess and post-tool hooks before returning to context
Inside each card, vertical down-arrows show an ordered sub-sequence of steps
visual_elements: Five rounded color-coded cards (blue, green, red, pink, blue) laid out horizontally
A distinct line-art icon centered above each card title (terminal, code+search, shield, person+speech bubble, checkmark)
Circular bullet markers with internal down-arrows listing each stage's steps
A thin horizontal divider line beneath each card's title
Looping connector lines with arrowheads arcing from the bottom of one card to the top of the next
key_points: A proposed tool call is never executed directly; it traverses a multi-stage safety pipeline first
The parser classifies commands by tier (read-only vs full/destructive) to decide how much trust to require
Active permission tiers such as Workspace Mode can satisfy the gate without any user interaction
Destructive or unknown commands escalate to an interactive prompt where the user can approve or deny
Every approved run is wrapped in pre- and post-tool hooks and audit logging, and the result is injected back into the agent context

title: Tsinghua NLAH Module Ablation Analysis
components: Tsinghua NLAH Module Ablation Results (left blue card)
Integration and Dependency Mapping (right blue card)
relationships: Top connector line runs from the left 'Ablation Results' card into the 'Harness Design Principle' card
Bottom connector line runs from the left 'Ablation Results' card into the 'Integration and Dependency Mapping' card
Inside the left card, vertical arrows chain the three bullets: Self-Evolution Attempt Loop -> Evaluation Verifiers -> Multi-Candidate Search
visual_elements: Three color-coded rounded cards (light blue, lavender, light blue) with thin outlines and header divider lines
Line-art header icons: bar/signal chart, stacked hexagons, and a connected node graph
Hollow-circle bullet markers next to each ablation row
Green check and red cross emoji flags marking 'CONSISTENTLY HELPS' vs 'HURTS PERFORMANCE'
Curved connector lines with arrowheads linking the left card to the two right cards
key_points: The Self-Evolution Attempt Loop is the only module that consistently improves both SWE-bench (+4.8) and OSWorld (+2.7)
Evaluation Verifiers (-0.8 / -8.4) and Multi-Candidate Search (-2.4 / -5.6) both hurt performance, so they are dropped
The distilled harness principle is 'Narrowing Attempt Loop > Broadening Search Space'
The integration rule is to fold Self-Evolution, Verifiers, and Search flow into a single Core Rule

title: AI Agent System Architecture Overview
relationships: No explicit arrows are drawn; the six boxes are presented as a flat horizontal peer row, so connections are conceptual rather than literal
Implied control flow: Loop & Execution Controller drives the LLM Engine and feeds its output back each turn
Implied data flow: Context Window holds the active prompt state that the LLM Engine reads and writes
Implied persistence: Context Window overflows to / is rehydrated from the External DB / State Files
Implied action path: LLM tool calls resolve through the Tool Registry and are gated by Permissions & Hooks before execution
visual_elements: Centered bold dark-gray heading 'AI Agent System Architecture' above a light off-white canvas
A single horizontal row of six evenly spaced shapes spanning the width of the frame
Most components rendered as light-blue rounded rectangles with cyan borders and blue label text
Context Window drawn as a left-flat blue cylinder and External DB / State Files as a green 3D database cylinder to distinguish memory types
Small gray 'Made with Napkin' watermark anchored in the bottom-right corner
key_points: The agent harness is the scaffolding around the model, not the model itself: the loop controller, context, tools and guardrails together form the harness
The context window is finite working memory, so external state files are required to persist and extend memory across turns and sessions
The Tool Registry decouples tool definitions from their execution, letting the LLM address tools by name
Permissions & Hooks act as an interception / safety layer that can approve, deny or modify any tool action before it runs
The Loop & Execution Controller is the engine room that orchestrates the read-prompt, call-LLM, dispatch-tool, append-result cycle

title: Framework vs Harness Paradigms in AI
relationships: Manual Wiring maps to Pre-Wired Engine
Custom App Pipeline maps to User Goal Execution
Building Blocks maps to Integrated Loop
Left column (framework approach) transforms into right column (harness approach) via three horizontal arrows
visual_elements: Two parallel columns of rounded rectangle boxes: orange-bordered on the left, red-bordered on the right
Three horizontal gray arrows pointing left-to-right pairing each orange box with a red box
Small gray caption text beneath every box explaining its meaning
Centered bold dark title at the top on a near-white background
Subtle 'Made with Napkin' watermark in the bottom-right corner
key_points: The framework paradigm (left) demands manual assembly of chains, retrievers, and state nodes, while the harness paradigm (right) ships a pre-configured engine ready to run.
Frameworks push developers to build bespoke application pipelines from scratch; harnesses instead target concrete user goals such as fixing issues.
Framework thinking is built from individual components (chains, retrievers) as building blocks, whereas harness thinking provides a continuous read-act-observe integrated loop.
The side-by-side contrast reframes agent engineering from wiring primitives to orchestrating a goal-driven execution loop.
